source_text: Cum praedicationis enumerat uarietatem, quod alii ei fiducia uinculorum eius audentius sermonem enuntiarent alii per inuidiam et contentionem, quidam uero et per sermonis existimationem, plerique ex dilectione, nonnulli ex aemulatione, iam aliqui et ex simultate Christum praedicarent, erat aliqui uel hic locus taxandae ipsius praedicationis de diuersitate sententiae, quae' tantam efficeret etiam animorum uarietatem. sed causas solas animorum, non regulas sacramentorum in diuersitate proponen, unum tamen Christum et unum eius deum quocumque consilio praedicatum confirmat et ideo: nihil mea, inquit, siue causatione eine ueritate Christus adnuntietur, quia unus adnuntiabatur siue ex cauastione siue ex ueritate fidei. ad fidem enim praedicationis retulit mentionem ueritatis, non ad regulae ipsius, quia una quidem erat regula, sed fides praedicantium.
pass_a_gloss: When he enumerates the variety of preaching, that some to him with the confidence of his bonds dare to proclaim a more confident sermon, others through envy and contention, certain ones indeed also through the estimation of the sermon, most out of love, some out of emulation, now some even out of hatred Christ preach, there was some place even here for censuring this preaching itself because of the diversity of opinion, which would bring about such a great variety of spirits. But he proposes only the causes of spirits, not the rules of sacraments in diversity, nevertheless he confirms one Christ and one God of his, preached with whatever counsel, and therefore: nothing is mine, he says, whether Christ is announced by my causation or by truth, because one Christ was being announced whether by causation or by truth of faith. For he referred the mention of truth to the faith of preaching, not to the rule itself, because there was one rule, but the faith of those preaching.

pass_b_english: When it comes to the variety of preaching, some people proclaim Christ with confidence because of their trust in His power, while others do so out of envy or rivalry, and a few even because they think it will enhance their reputation. Most preach out of love, some out of a desire to compete, and a few - surprisingly - out of hatred. This diversity of motivations raises questions about the preaching itself, given the wide range of opinions and emotions at play. However, the focus here is on the underlying motivations, not on the rules governing sacraments. The key point is that, regardless of the motivation, the message is about one Christ and one God. As the author puts it, it doesn't matter whether Christ is proclaimed for personal reasons or out of a commitment to truth - the fact remains that only one Christ is being proclaimed, whether the proclamation is driven by personal motives or by a genuine faith. The emphasis is on the faith of those doing the preaching, not on the rules they follow, because when it comes to the core message, there's only one standard, but the faith of the preachers can vary greatly. The bottom line is that the authenticity of the preaching depends on the preachers' faith, not on their motivations or methods.

review.notes: Pass B is a paraphrase/interpretation rather than a translation. It adds significant content and interpretive conclusions not present in the Latin source, such as 'This diversity of motivations raises questions about the preaching itself, given the wide range of opinions and emotions at play' and 'The bottom line is that the authenticity of the preaching depends on the preachers' faith, not on their motivations or methods.' These additions violate the rule that Pass B must neither add to nor contradict Pass A or the Greek. Additionally, Pass A translates 'simultate' as 'hatred' (matching the lemma provided), but Pass B translates it as 'surprisingly - out of hatred', adding an adverbial layer not in the source.
